gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: The old system charged per download, ___ the new one uses a flat monthly fee.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' sets the old and new systems side by side.

gaps.sentence: She has decided to cycle to work ___ taking the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' = in place of the bus journey.

gaps.sentence: ___ her brother, she took to skiing almost immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'Unlike + noun' is a preposition phrase contrasting two people.

gaps.sentence: ___ keep the audience engaged, the lecturer used live demonstrations.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'In order to + infinitive' states the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: We went for a long walk ___ it was drizzling.
gaps.explanation: Only the conjunction 'even though' can introduce the finite clause 'it was drizzling'.

gaps.sentence: He went back inside, ___ the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the danger' — noun phrase; although needs a clause.
